title: Breast lump removal (lumpectomy)
what: The surgeon removes the lump in the breast along with a small area of tissue. The tissue is sent to the lab.
why: When a lump is found in the breast that needs to be removed or studied closely under a microscope.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; you often go home the same day or the next
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding
If the lump is hard to feel, it may be marked before surgery

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Marker
prepare.text: If the lump is small, it may be marked the day before or that morning, using ultrasound or a mammogram.

bring: Your mammogram, ultrasound, and biopsy results
steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
The anesthetist gives general anesthesia, or the area is numbed
The surgeon makes a cut, often along the edge of the areola or in a skin fold
The lump is removed with a small area of tissue
The wound is closed with a cosmetic stitch
feel: The breast aches for a few days. You will get painkillers
There may be a bruise and a firm area at the scar
Feeling anxious about the result is normal. Ask when it will be ready
after: A comfortable supportive bra reduces pain
Keep the dressing dry until you are told it is OK
Lab results are usually ready in 1 to 2 weeks
Your doctor will explain the result at your visit
red_flags: The breast becomes much bigger, tight, and blue
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus from the wound

faq.q: Will the shape of my breast change?
faq.a: Usually only a little. The surgeon tries to keep the shape and hide the scar.

faq.q: Does surgery mean it is cancer?
faq.a: No. Lumps are often benign. The lab results will give the answer.

reminders.text: Breast surgery tomorrow. Bring your scans and a comfortable bra. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
